about.label: (01) About
about.title: I'm Iury. I learn by building — and build to learn.
about.lead: Most of what I make starts as a question I can't stop thinking about. This portfolio is where I document what I find.

traits.text: AI is my main material right now — assistants, agents and tools that make information genuinely useful.
I care about how things feel, not only how they work. The interface is part of the solution.
I'd rather ship an honest prototype than polish a guess. Every project teaches something specific.

approach.label: (04) Approach
approach.title: How a question becomes a thing.
approach.note: Five moves, in order — then again. The last step feeds the first.

steps.title: Observe
steps.text: Notice what people actually do, not what they say they do.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Find the real question under the request.

steps.title: Experiment
steps.text: Build the smallest thing that can prove me wrong.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Turn what survived into something people can use.

steps.title: Improve
steps.text: Ship, watch, adjust — and start observing again.

home.greeting: Hi — I'm the cat. I know a few things about Iury. What would you like to know?

chips.label: Who is Iury?
chips.answer: An IT Assistant at Giassi Supermercados, working with SQL, PL/SQL and Oracle. He studies Computer Science (UNESC) and Systems Analysis and Development (UNOPAR). He learns by building — and this site is where he documents what he finds.

chips.label: AI experience?
chips.answer: The most complete case is Koinonia: a live product built with AI, where Iury defined the problem, wrote the directives, orchestrated the build and tested the result. At work he uses AI to write rules and automations on the DOX platform.

home.fallback: I'm still a prototype: scripted answers, no language model behind them. Try one of the suggestions.

koinonia.greeting: I've read this case study. Ask me why a Radar, how AI was used or what the audit found.

chips.label: Why a Radar?
chips.answer: Because an attendance list says who came, not where to start. The Radar ranks people by risk of drifting away and turns it into a care queue — without flagging newcomers as at risk.

chips.label: How was AI used?
chips.answer: AI wrote the code from a brief and plans Iury wrote. He directed every round, checked the result and tested it on desktop and mobile.

chips.label: What did the audit find?
chips.answer: Silent failures: unpaginated reads that would have broken the Radar past a thousand records, an inverted date filter that hid people who needed care, and no tests. All fixed.

koinonia.fallback: About this project I can only answer the suggestions above — I'm still a scripted prototype.
